metadata.headline: How can Airbnb offer millions of places to stay without building hotels?

platform_lesson.title: Airbnb grows accommodation supply by helping existing homes become bookable
platform_lesson.text: A hotel company usually grows by building, buying or operating more rooms. Airbnb can grow differently. Hosts make homes, apartments and rooms available on the platform, while guests search and book them through Airbnb. This lets Airbnb offer a very large accommodation network without owning the homes itself. The difficult part is trust. A spare room is only useful supply if a host is willing to let a stranger stay there and a guest is willing to book a home they have never seen. Airbnb therefore adds identity verification, reviews, reservation screening, payments, support and AirCover around the booking. The platform scales by organizing homes that already exist and making the transaction between host and guest easier and safer.

sources.title: About us — Airbnb fast facts
sources.note: Airbnb reports 9M+ active listings, 5.5M+ hosts, 150K+ cities and towns, 220+ countries and regions, and 2.5B+ guest arrivals all-time.

sources.title: Airbnb 2025 Annual Report
sources.note: Reports 533M Nights and Seats Booked and $91.3B Gross Booking Value for 2025 and explains Airbnb's platform metrics and business model.

sources.title: Airbnb Q2 2026 Form 10-Q
sources.note: Reports 148M Nights and Seats Booked and $27.25B Gross Booking Value in Q2 2026; Airbnb notes that substantially all bookings to date have come from nights.

sources.title: Airbnb service fees
sources.note: Describes the split-fee and single-fee structures and states that Airbnb is transitioning home hosts away from the split-fee structure.

sources.title: Simplifying Airbnb service fees
sources.note: Explains Airbnb's 2026 move toward a single 15.5% host-paid service fee for affected hosts, replacing the older split-fee model.

sources.title: AirCover for Hosts
sources.note: AirCover includes guest identity verification, reservation screening, $3M Host damage protection, $1M Host liability insurance and a 24-hour safety line.

sources.title: Host Liability Insurance Program Summary
sources.note: Airbnb states that Host liability insurance is underwritten by third-party insurers; regional arrangements and terms vary.

sources.title: Airbnb Global Quality Report
sources.note: Describes Airbnb's quality and trust systems and says more than 400,000 low-quality listings had been removed as part of quality improvements.

core_value_unit.explanation: The core value exchanged is a bookable stay in a host's home, apartment, room or other accommodation.

metrics.note: Airbnb reported 148 million Nights and Seats Booked in Q2 2026. Substantially all bookings to date have come from nights, but this metric also includes Experiences and Services seats.

actor.explanation: Airbnb operates the marketplace, search and booking system, payment flow, trust systems and support that connect hosts with guests.

job.explanation: Airbnb has to make a very large, distributed supply of homes easy to discover, compare, book and trust.

gain.explanation: More useful supply attracts more guest demand, while more demand makes hosting more attractive and generates service-fee revenue for Airbnb.

pain.explanation: Airbnb must manage fraud, unsafe stays, inconsistent quality, cancellations, local regulation and disputes even though it does not own the homes.

transaction.explanation: Airbnb coordinates discovery, booking, payment, payout, messaging and support around the stay.

governance.explanation: Listing standards, guest rules, reviews, verification, reservation screening and enforcement shape participation and behavior on the platform.

promotion_channel.explanation: Airbnb attracts demand through its app and website, search engines, direct brand traffic, referrals and marketing.

activities.explanation: Airbnb runs search and ranking, processes bookings and payments, supports users, manages safety systems and helps resolve problems.

resources.explanation: Core resources include the host network, guest demand, listing data, reviews, search and ranking systems, payment infrastructure and the Airbnb brand.

metrics.note: Airbnb reports active listings in more than 220 countries and regions.

actor.explanation: Guests are travelers looking for a place to stay, from private rooms and apartments to whole homes and other accommodation types.

job.explanation: Guests want accommodation that fits their destination, dates, budget, group and preferences.

gain.explanation: Guests can access many different types of places and locations, often with more variety than a single hotel chain can offer.

pain.explanation: Guests may worry about total price, misleading listings, cancellations, cleanliness, safety or whether a home will match its description.

transaction.explanation: Guests search, compare, book and pay through Airbnb, then review the stay afterward.

filter.explanation: Guests filter by destination, dates, price, type of home, amenities, reviews and other preferences.

access_channel.explanation: Guests access the marketplace through Airbnb's mobile app and website.

activities.explanation: Guests search, compare, message hosts when needed, book, stay and leave ratings or reviews.

resources.explanation: Guests bring travel demand, dates, destination, budget, identity information and reviews from past stays.

metrics.note: Airbnb reports more than 2.5 billion guest arrivals all-time; this is cumulative, not a current active-user count.

actor.explanation: Hosts range from individuals sharing a room or home to professional property managers and hospitality operators listing accommodations on Airbnb.

job.explanation: Hosts want to turn available space into income while controlling dates, pricing, house rules and how they host.

gain.explanation: Airbnb gives hosts access to global traveler demand, booking tools and a recognizable marketplace brand.

pain.explanation: Hosts face property damage, cancellations, difficult guests, local rules, taxes, cleaning work and the risk of poor reviews.

transaction.explanation: Hosts create listings, set availability and prices, accept or automatically receive bookings, provide the stay and receive payouts.

filter.explanation: Listings and hosts are subject to platform standards, reviews, verification processes and local legal requirements where applicable.

access_channel.explanation: Hosts use Airbnb's hosting dashboard, app, calendar, pricing tools, messaging, payout settings and support.

activities.explanation: Hosts prepare and describe the space, manage availability, communicate with guests, provide the stay and maintain quality.

resources.explanation: Hosts contribute the physical accommodation, availability, local knowledge, hospitality work and the quality of the stay.

metrics.note: Airbnb reports more than 5.5 million hosts worldwide as of May 2026.
Airbnb reports more than 9 million active listings worldwide as of May 2026.

actor.explanation: Third-party insurers underwrite Airbnb's Host liability insurance in participating countries, adding an external risk-bearing layer to AirCover for Hosts.

job.explanation: Insurance partners cover eligible host liability claims when a host is legally responsible for guest injury or property damage, subject to policy terms.

gain.explanation: Airbnb's global host network creates large recurring insurance exposure and policy volume for underwriting partners.

pain.explanation: Insurers must manage claims, exclusions, fraud, changing regulation and different legal conditions across markets.

transaction.explanation: Airbnb arranges liability coverage for eligible hosts and insurers underwrite and handle covered claims according to local policy terms.

filter.explanation: Coverage depends on the host's location, eligible activity and the terms, conditions and exclusions of the applicable policy.

access_channel.explanation: The liability-insurance layer is delivered to eligible hosts through Airbnb's AirCover for Hosts program.

activities.explanation: Insurance partners underwrite eligible risk, evaluate claims and pay covered liabilities under the applicable policy.

resources.explanation: Partners contribute regulated underwriting capability, claims expertise and capital that Airbnb does not need to hold itself.

metrics.note: AirCover for Hosts includes $1 million of Host liability insurance in eligible countries, subject to policy terms and exclusions.
Airbnb reports more than 9 million active listings worldwide as of May 2026.
Airbnb reports more than 5.5 million hosts worldwide as of May 2026.
Airbnb reported 148 million Nights and Seats Booked in Q2 2026. Substantially all bookings to date have come from nights, but the metric also includes Experiences and Services seats.

current.explanation: Guests bring travel demand to Airbnb, search the marketplace and pay through the platform when they book.
Airbnb gives guests searchable listings, booking tools, payments, messaging, reviews and customer support.
Hosts make accommodation supply visible by listing homes or rooms, setting availability, prices and house rules.
Airbnb brings guest demand to hosts, manages bookings and sends host payouts after applying the applicable service-fee structure.
The host provides the actual accommodation that the guest booked through Airbnb.
Third-party insurers provide the liability-insurance layer included in AirCover for eligible hosts in participating markets.
